alt: A grid comparing modernisation, dependency, world systems, neoliberal and people-centred theories: why each thinks poor countries are poor, its route to development, and a key criticism.
caption: Each theory locates the cause of poverty somewhere different.

alt: Five rising steps: traditional society, preconditions for take-off, take-off, drive to maturity, and the age of high mass consumption. Western aid and investment are meant to help societies reach take-off.
caption: Modernisation theory sees one path to development, with Western help at take-off.

alt: Left: Frank’s model, with surplus flowing from four satellites to the metropolis. Right: Wallerstein’s world system as rings of core, semi-periphery and periphery, with countries able to move between them.
caption: Wallerstein adds a middle zone and mobility to Frank’s two-part model.

alt: Three measures from narrow to wide: GNI per capita, which hides inequality and unpaid work; the Human Development Index, combining life expectancy, education and income; and Sen’s view of development as real freedoms.
caption: Each measure widens what counts as development.

alt: A spectrum from hyperglobalists (Ohmae), through transformationalists (Held and colleagues), to sceptics (Hirst and Thompson). Below, Ritzer’s McDonaldization is set against glocalisation and South-to-North cultural flows.
caption: Transformationalists take the middle view: globalisation is real but uneven.

after: ## 4. Aid and trade, industrialisation and urbanisation
alt: Arguments that aid helps, from modernisation theory, Sachs and humanitarian relief, set against Hayter’s and Moyo’s arguments that it serves donors and breeds dependency. Collier’s four development traps are listed beneath.
caption: The debate is mainly about long-term state-to-state aid, not emergency relief.

after: ## 5. The environment, and war and conflict
alt: A cycle in which war and conflict cause damage, damage causes poverty, and poverty raises the risk of further war. Side panels list the damage conflict does and Kaldor’s idea of "new wars".
caption: War causes poverty, and poverty raises the risk of war.
